sources.note: Sociolinguistic summary only (c. 3,000 signers, Honiara deaf community, Auslan/Signed English admixture); sole reference is the ISO 639-3 change request. Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Reed, Lauren W. 2019. Sign languages of Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea, and their challenges for sign language typology. MA thesis, Australian National University. 167 pp. hdl:1885/165444
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not about SISL. Mentions the Solomons only for Kagobai's Rennell Island sign language (Kuschel 1973, 1974; a different language, ISO rsi) and cites Reed & Rumsey (in press). No statement on SISL prosody or stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2016. Change Request 2016-013: create [szs] Solomon Islands Sign Language (submitted by D. Adone, A. Barnabas, B. Macpherson; adopted 2017-01-31). 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or prosody; notes syntax/classifier/non-manual differences from Auslan and states 'No published source on SISL to our knowledge' (p. 4); the only work named is Laloga, Leve, Moli, Macpherson & Adone (in prep.) on the ecology of SISL.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2016. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: szs Solomon Islands Sign Language (Adone & Macpherson). 4 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; sociolinguistic profile only (Honiara hub, Malaita vs Guadalcanal sign variation, Auslan/Signed English admixture, 'mouth gestures' influenced by Auslan); repeats 'No published source on SISL to our knowledge' (p. 4).
